issues.what: Three smoke runs (12:45-12:53 UTC) evaluated synthetic rules drawn from the real vocabulary on the real labelled halves with the real cell family and real round-0 rules, with the ledger redirected to the scratchpad (unlogged trials, contrary to 'every configuration you evaluate is a ledger row'); the max-T statistic was then switched from the Welch t to pooled_z after seeing the strict smoke's real-data null (p95 of max|t| 10.6 vs 5.76), which makes the test easier to pass; one synthetic rule (`n_choch_since_bos >= 2 and dir == up`) is identical to the later r1B_m7 (same z -1.391 on half A). Disclosed in NOTES.md; happened before any round-1 rule existed; no rule came near eligibility under either statistic, so the null stands.
issues.where: studies/llm_round1/NOTES.md 'Code smoke test' section; smoke_logs/smoke_strict_1.log line 12 (null p95 10.635) vs smoke_relax_1_no_selection.log line 12 (5.756); scorer.py lines 636-667 (smoke) and 657-661 (synthetic rules); FINDINGS.md section 8 last paragraph
issues.evidence: smoke_strict_1.log: '[B->A minute] ... rules: sB_minute_1 t 3.183 fw_p 0.9845' (real half A labels, Welch); smoke_relax_1: 'sB_minute_2 t -1.391' == scorer.log line 42 'r1B_m7 t -1.391'. NOTES.md states the statistic change was made 'BEFORE any round-1 rule existed'. Round-1 best fw p under pooled_z is 0.1449 and wrong-signed, so the choice of statistic does not change the verdict.
issues.fix: Record the smoke-test evaluations as a caveat in FINDINGS section 11 (count: 16 testable synthetic rules x L1/L0 x 3 runs, unlogged) and note that the statistic change was made after a real-data look at the null distribution; in future run smoke tests on permuted labels or synthetic nets, never on the real book.
